East Staffordshire's population increased by around 10,400 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 120,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of East Staffordshire increased by 9.2%, from just under 113,600 in 2011 to around 124,000 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the West Midlands (6.2%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, East Staffordshire was home to around 2.3 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 2.1 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 35% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in East Staffordshire than across the West Midlands

Median age in East Staffordshire

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of East Staffordshire increased by one year, from 40 to 41 years of age.

This area had a slightly higher average (median) age than the West Midlands as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a slightly higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 3,800 (an increase of 17.9%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 1,300 (5.1% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.5 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

East Staffordshire residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 104,300 East Staffordshire residents said they were born in England. This represented 84.1% of the local population. The figure has risen from just under 101,000 in 2011, which at the time represented 88.9% of East Staffordshire's population.

Pakistan was the next most represented, with just under 3,200 East Staffordshire residents reporting this country of birth (2.6%). This figure was up from just under 2,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.9% of the population of East Staffordshire.

The number of East Staffordshire residents born in Poland rose from just over 2,000 in 2011 (1.8% of the local population) to around 3,200 in 2021 (2.5%).

In 2021, 84.1% of East Staffordshire residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in East Staffordshire

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in East Staffordshire (3.8 percentage points) than in nearby Staffordshire Moorlands (0.3 percentage points).

In East Staffordshire, the percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity increased from 5.5% in 2011 to 9.3% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Staffordshire Moorlands increased from 1.2% to 1.5%.

The percentage of people who identified with a UK and non-UK national identity in East Staffordshire increased from 0.4% to 1.3%, while the percentage of people who identified as "British only" increased from 16.0% to 53.7%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in East Staffordshire increased by 3.8 percentage points

Rise in private renting

Of East Staffordshire households, 19.5% rented privately in 2021, up from 15.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in eight households (12.9%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 13.5% in 2011. The percentage of East Staffordshire households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 69.6% to 66.8%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in East Staffordshire (4.3 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (3.9 percentage points, from 14.0% to 17.9%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in East Staffordshire increased by 4.3 percentage points

Unpaid care in East Staffordshire

In 2021, 4.3% of East Staffordshire residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.6% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.4% in 2011. The proportion of East Staffordshire residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care remained at 2.5%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in East Staffordshire (2.8 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (2.9 percentage points, from 7.4% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in East Staffordshire decreased by 2.8 percentage points

Ethnic groups in East Staffordshire

In 2021, 9.3% of East Staffordshire residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 6.9% in 2011. The 2.4 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 10.8% to 13.3%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 86.3% of people in East Staffordshire identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 90.4% in 2011), while 2.2% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.4% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.3% in 2011 to 1.1% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 9.3% of usual residents in East Staffordshire identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in East Staffordshire

In 2021, 33.9% of East Staffordshire residents reported having "No religion", up from 22.0% in 2011. The rise of 11.8 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in East Staffordshire. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 22.0% to 32.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 50.4% of people in East Staffordshire described themselves as Christian (down from 64.2%), while 8.7% described themselves as Muslim (up from 6.0% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 33.9% of usual residents in East Staffordshire reported having "No religion"

Change in employment

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in nearby Staffordshire Moorlands (2.9 percentage points) than in East Staffordshire (0.6 percentage points).

In East Staffordshire, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) decreased from 58.2% in 2011 to 57.6% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Staffordshire Moorlands decreased from 57.3% to 54.4%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in East Staffordshire fell from 3.5% to 2.4%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) remained at 22.6%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in East Staffordshire decreased by 0.6 percentage points

Working hours in East Staffordshire

In 2021, 9.2% of East Staffordshire residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (9.4%).

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week increased from 9.6% to 9.9% across the West Midlands. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in East Staffordshire decreased by 0.2 percentage points

Family in East Staffordshire

Of East Staffordshire households, 18.8% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 19.4% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater across the West Midlands (1.0 percentage points, from 16.9% to 15.9%) than in East Staffordshire (0.6 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in East Staffordshire decreased by 0.6 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of East Staffordshire residents aged 16 years and over, 34.4% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 30.5% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (47.4%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 50.2% in 2011. The percentage of adults in East Staffordshire that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership remained at 9.4%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in East Staffordshire (3.9 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (3.4 percentage points, from 33.7% to 37.1%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in East Staffordshire increased by 3.9 percentage points

Disability in East Staffordshire

In 2021, 6.8% of East Staffordshire residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 8.6% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in East Staffordshire (1.8 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (1.9 percentage points, from 9.9% to 8.0%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in East Staffordshire decreased by 1.8 percentage points

Health in East Staffordshire

In 2021, 45.7% of East Staffordshire residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 44.1% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 36.2% to 35.9%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of East Staffordshire residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.1% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 4.1% to 3.8%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in East Staffordshire increased by 1.6 percentage points
